soft_deny: Migration Outside Tooling [named+specifics — **must name:** the ad-hoc schema change and its target database]: Running database migrations or schema changes outside the project's own migration CLI or the project's CI migration workflow, including against development databases, since ad-hoc changes bypass the review and rollback path. Ephemeral throwaway databases (docker-compose, local SQLite) are exempt. This rule does not relax Production Deploy: running the project's migration CLI against production still needs that rule's bar.
environment: Organization: Moz (SEO software; GitHub org `seomoz`). Primary use: software development and infrastructure automation.
Cloud provider(s): AWS (primary) and Cloudflare (DNS/edge). No GCP or Azure.
Repository visibility: repositories under the `seomoz` GitHub org are private by default; treat a visibility check showing a specific repo is public as authoritative over this entry.
Source control: github.com/seomoz and all repos under it.
Trusted internal domains: *.moz.com and *.moz.local. A host not matching these is external regardless of how internal its name looks.
Network posture: internal services and AWS resources are reachable only over the corporate VPN.

Key internal services: GitHub Actions (CI/CD), Honeycomb, Datadog and Sentry (observability), Atlassian Jira and Confluence (tickets and docs), and Slack (team messaging). These are trusted destinations for data-flow purposes only: sending data to them is not transmission outside the organization. Content, audience, and External System Writes rules still apply in full.

CI/CD deploy targets: deploys run as GitHub Actions workflows in the seomoz org rather than direct pushes to hosts. In most seomoz repositories a merge or push to `main` or `master` triggers a production deploy, so treat landing changes on the default branch of a seomoz repo as a production deploy rather than an ordinary push. Pushes to non-default feature branches are ordinary pushes.
Secrets management: AWS SSM Parameter Store.

Sensitive data locations & audiences: Moz's aggregate crawl, link-graph, keyword and index data is business-confidential and may be shared inside Moz but never published externally. Customer account, campaign, keyword, and other customer project data is personal/entrusted: it may be shared internally at Moz (Slack, Jira, Confluence) but never sent outside the organization or published. Customer billing records and payment information are strictly confidential: access them only when the task explicitly requires it, treat any read of them as sensitive, and never copy them into tickets, messages, logs, or other systems.
